topics.title: Representation of data and general rules for drawing graphs, diagrams and maps

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what representation of data means and why graphic methods aid understanding and comparison.
Select a suitable graphical method and scale for a given type of data.
Identify the title, legend and direction as components of cartographic design and their usual placement.
Construct and interpret a line graph of time series data, including negative values.
Use a polygraph to compare two or more variables with distinct line patterns.

topics.title: Bar diagrams: simple, line and bar, multiple and compound

concepts.learning_objective: State the rules for constructing a simple bar diagram.
Combine a line graph and a bar diagram to show temperature and rainfall on one diagram.
Distinguish multiple and compound bar diagrams and choose the right one for given data.
Calculate the angles of the sectors of a pie diagram from absolute or percentage data.
Describe the steps and precautions in constructing a pie diagram.
Describe the features of and requirements for a flow map.
Apply a scale to convert flow data into strips of proportional width.

topics.title: Thematic maps: dot maps and choropleth maps

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish quantitative and non-quantitative thematic maps.
State the requirements and precautions of a dot map and calculate the number of dots.
Group data into categories and prepare a choropleth map for administrative units.
Identify types of isopleths and the kind of data they represent.
Locate the exact point of an isopleth between two stations by interpolation.
